Custom Agents are AI teammates that automate your busywork. Here are five tips to build your first one: Pick one task you do repeatedly (tagging, routing, weekly recaps) Write clear instructions: the goal, the format, and what to do when it's unsure Add a trigger (on a schedule or when X happens) so it runs in the background Start with the minimum permissions it needs. You can expand later. Test run → tweak → test again.

Have you ever zoned out on a Zoom call, then realised you’ve missed the last two minutes? I’ve been trying Wispr Flow’s Notetaker, which records and transcribes meetings in real time. You can ask it what you missed, search previous meetings for specific decisions, and use the transcripts with tools like ChatGPT and Claude to draft follow-up emails or messages. Very useful if, like me, you spend a lot of time in meetings, and even more time trying to remember what actually happened in them.  It’s currently available on Mac and Windows, and the Notetaker is free to use. Copy the link for one month of Wispr Flow Pro for free: https://ref.wisprflow.ai/ali_tiktok_notetaker

Women deserve to know their options for treating vaginal dryness and painful sex. On unPAUSED, we discuss low-dose vaginal estrogen and its role in treating genitourinary syndrome of menopause, or GSM. If lubricants are the only option you’ve been offered, ask whether vaginal estrogen could be appropriate for you. You deserve a conversation about your symptoms and the treatments available. ✨Listen to the full episode at the link in my bio.  #menopause #womenshealth #midlife #hormonehealth #perimenopause

That is part of my “why.” Why I lift weights. Why I move my body. Why I pay attention to nutrition, sleep, and the supplements I choose based on my individual needs. There are no guarantees. A UTI can become much more than a urinary problem for older women. On unPAUSED, we discuss how these infections can become serious and potentially lead to sepsis. We also explore a possible connection between infection-related confusion, falls, and hip fractures. A woman who becomes confused, tries to get out of bed to use the bathroom, and falls may be facing more than one health crisis at once. It’s a conversation that shows why urinary health deserves more attention as women age. ✨Listen to the full conversation at the link in my bio.  #uti #womenshealth #menopause #hormonehealth #healthcare

Using “warming” lube? More ingredients don’t necessarily mean a better experience. On this episode of unPAUSED I dive into everything you need to know about GSM, and answer your most asked questions. Including why peppermint oil, fragrance, and unnecessary extras can make discomfort worse, especially when vaginal tissue is already irritated. The takeaway here: keep it simple. Look for fragrance-free products with as few ingredients as possible. You don’t need all the bells and whistles in your lubricant. ✨Listen to the full episode at the link in bio.  #menopause #gsm #vaginalhealth #midlife #womenshealth

I’ve been a physician for decades, and this one surprised me. Dense breasts don’t just make cancer harder to spot on a mammogram. They also raise your risk of breast cancer. About half of women have dense breasts, and many don’t know what that means for their screening. This week on unPAUSED, breast oncologist, Eleonora Teplinsky, MD breaks down when to ask your doctor about an MRI or ultrasound. ✨Listen to the full episode at the link in bio.  #breastcancer #breastcancerawareness #breastcancersupport  #womenshealth #healthcare

Menopause weight gain isn’t a willpower problem. Your scale can barely move while your body changes underneath it: more fat around your organs, less muscle, and an appetite system working against you. A review published in September in the International Journal of Molecular Sciences pulls together 25 years of research on what falling estrogen does to appetite. Estrogen helps run the hunger switch in the hypothalamus; when it falls, the balance tips toward hunger. Leptin, the hormone that tells your brain you’ve had enough, rises, but the brain responds to it less. Ghrelin, your hunger hormone, dips after a meal but climbs back faster.
